arabic_locator.text: وَعَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْبَاقِرِ: ﴿وَانْحَرْ﴾ يَعْنِي: ارْفَعِ الْيَدَيْنِ عِنْدَ افْتِتَاحِ الصَّلَاةِ.

semantic_candidate.statement_en: Ibn Kathir reports from Abu Jafar al-Baqir an interpretation of wanhar as raising both hands at the opening of prayer.

fidelity_notes: ارفع اليدين specifies both hands; عند افتتاح الصلاة limits this interpretation to the opening of prayer.
This is an interpretation attributed to al-Baqir; the imperative inside it does not make Ibn Kathir its commanding speaker.
Abu Jafar al-Baqir is distinct from Abu Jafar ibn Jarir named later; do not merge their identities.
A01's immediately adjacent la yasihh criticism is not attached to this al-Baqir attribution.
English statement is analytical paraphrase of Arabic, not quotation from corresponding abridged English witness.
disagreement: Hand-raising interpretation differs from the sacrificial-slaughter reading later preferred by Ibn Kathir; no new authentication or independent witness claimed.
